Hi,

Thanks for your feedback.

Github repository link: https://github.com/rickavila/opensci.uap . Yes, all of my open UAP video recordings include date time and anything else the iphone captures like GPS coordinates.

Allsky cameras typically are set up with some automatic exposure settings. On dark sky nights the camera I showed was set up for 10 second exposures. However, there were a lot of clouds on the night I showed with the strange object (white curved line with two blue dots) in between clouds. So the automatic exposure setting kicked in and brought the exposure time down to 2.3 seconds. The frame I showed with the strange object had a total exposure of 2.3 seconds.

My allsky camera now has a nice big lens on it and I can now get 5 second exposures throughout a dark sky night, even here in light pollution infested Albany area.

The only thing that showed some potential for strange properties that I recorded that night on my night vision scope was this very fast moving object I showed. I was surprised that nothing showed up on the allsky camera - but maybe the object seen in the night vision scope was moving too fast. As I said in the video, not sure what that object could be but it doesn't have enough highly anomalous features to be called a UAP in my book.

I have lots of other night vision recordings of "interesting" things, but nothing truly compelling (yet - I can hope right?).

- Rick

PS: I keep posting replies on this platform but they keep disappearing - very strange. Not sure why that is happening.

My response to Mick West: Thanks for catching some poor wording. I fixed it in the post. I have no idea wha these UAP objects are. I hope one day we find out.
